children: U.S. stocks can keep advancing as corporate profits grow, but investors should be cautious about chasing recent winners as market leadership remains unusually concentrated, according to Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider and his team.

In their Oct. 16 report, the strategists argue that slowing economic and earnings growth should temper equity returns rather than end the rally. Their preferred opportunities include consumer-facing stocks that have lagged, supported by an expected improvement in household purchasing power in 2027.
The warning lies beneath the market’s headline performance. At the time of the report, the S&P 500 (
) stood just 2% below its record high, while the median constituent was 15% below its own high. Goldman’s measure of market breadth was near its narrowest level since the dot-com bubble.

That gap creates a problem for momentum strategies, which favor recent outperformers. Market participation could broaden as laggards recover, or leading stocks could fall toward the rest of the market. Either development could reverse the trades that benefited from the previous leadership.
Goldman’s momentum factor fell 8% during the week covered by the report, illustrating how quickly those positions can unwind.
Earnings remain supportive
Goldman forecasts S&P 500 (

) earnings per share of $375 in 2026 and $415 in 2027, representing reported growth of 36% and 11%, respectively. Adjusting for nonrecurring accounting distortions, the bank puts growth at 29% this year and 18% next year.
The distinction matters: the underlying profit outlook remains solid even as the pace slows.

Higher interest rates and oil prices are expected to restrain economic activity. Meanwhile, the earnings boost from artificial intelligence investment should diminish as spending growth moderates and depreciation expenses increase. Goldman estimates that AI capital spending currently accounts for roughly half of S&P 500 earnings growth.

The strategists also see less scope for the large upward earnings revisions that have supported stocks. Their 2027 forecast is close to analysts’ aggregate estimate, while their 2028 forecast of $460 a share is approximately 7% below consensus.

Early third-quarter results offer tentative support for that more measured outlook. With only 10% of S&P 500 companies having reported, 53% had exceeded consensus earnings by more than one standard deviation of analyst estimates. That was above the 25-year average of 50%, but below the 64% average over the preceding four quarters.
Consumer laggards offer potential opening

Goldman’s consumer thesis rests on falling inflation, lower energy prices and lower interest rates in 2027. Together, those developments should lift inflation-adjusted income growth, particularly among lower-income households.

The bank forecasts real income growth for the bottom income fifth accelerating from 0.4% in 2026 to 1.8% in 2027, measured from fourth quarter to fourth quarter. January cost-of-living adjustments to transfer payments should provide additional support.

Positioning could help a recovery. Goldman’s prime brokerage data showed hedge fund exposure to consumer discretionary stocks at multiyear lows, suggesting investors had already pulled back substantially from the sector.

A Goldman basket of discretionary stocks exposed to lower-income consumers had gained 7% since the start of October. The strategists also favor companies tied to consumer experiences, citing durable growth prospects and undemanding valuations.
That preference is selective. Historically, consumer discretionary stocks as a whole have tended to underperform when economic growth remains positive but slows.
Tougher environment for stock selection

Past periods of positive but decelerating growth have generally delivered further S&P 500 gains, Goldman’s analysis shows. Those returns have relied more on earnings increases than on investors paying higher valuations.

Such conditions have typically favored businesses with durable growth drivers, improving earnings estimates and lower share-price volatility. Snider’s team expects companies delivering accelerating profit growth to command a premium as that characteristic becomes scarcer.

The risk is that the slowdown deepens. Rising funding costs have already weighed on economically sensitive shares and parts of the AI trade, while hedge funds have reduced exposure. Goldman’s cyclical-versus-defensive stock pair fell 6% over the two weeks preceding the report.

For investors, the bank’s outlook supports continued equity exposure with greater attention to earnings resilience, valuation and positioning. Further gains remain plausible, but the stocks that led the market higher may face a more difficult path.

title: Goldman Sachs sees room for stocks to rise, warns not to chase market leaders
